title: Practice: Design a Music Player
summary: A Spotify-style player done step by step: library and playlists, a State-pattern player, a play queue with shuffle and repeat, observers, audio device selection through adapters, and the track-ended race.

steps.title: Clarify the requirements
hints: "Music player" can mean a streaming service (system design) or the player object (LLD). Pin that down first.
Walk through what a user does with the buttons: play, pause, next, previous, shuffle, repeat. Each one is a requirement.
Where does the sound come out? Ask what happens when the user picks another device mid-song, and when that device disconnects.
checklist: Scope pinned: in-process player and library, not a streaming backend
Library, playlists and a play queue
Playback controls including previous's "restart if > 3s" behaviour
Shuffle and repeat (off / one / all) semantics
Something that reacts to playback: UI, now-playing, scrobbling
Audio device selection: list devices, switch mid-song keeping position and play/pause, fall back to the speaker and pause on disconnect

steps.title: Identify entities and enums
hints: Separate **catalog** objects (song, album, playlist) from **playback** objects (queue, player, output).
Is a playlist the same thing as the queue? What happens to the playlist when you shuffle?
A device in the picker (name, type) is not the same thing as the object that plays audio on it. Which entity maps one to the other?
checklist: Song as an immutable value object; Album/Artist/Playlist in the catalog
PlayQueue separate from Playlist
Player with an explicit state
RepeatMode enum, and an AudioOutput abstraction
AudioDevice + DeviceType, one adapter per device SDK, and a DeviceManager for the connected devices

steps.title: Draw the class diagram
hints: The Player is the context object. What does it *own* and what does it *use*?
Which collaborators are interfaces so you can swap them in tests?
checklist: Player → PlayQueue, PlayerState, AudioOutput, listeners
Playlist holds song references, the queue holds playback order
Interfaces: PlayerState, AudioOutput, PlayerListener
Multiplicities (playlist * — * song)
Adapters (Cast, Bluetooth) wrapping vendor SDKs; DeviceManager owned by Player

steps.title: Model the player as a state machine
hints: Draw a table with the states as rows and the buttons as columns. Fill every cell.
If the cells are full of `if (state == …)` checks spread over many methods, that's the signal for the State pattern.
Add a "switch device" column. Does switching do the same thing when stopped, playing and paused?
checklist: States STOPPED, PLAYING, PAUSED (BUFFERING as an extension)
Every (state, action) pair defined, including the no-ops
State pattern: one class per state, each returning the next state
Side effects (start/pause audio) happen in the transition
A switch-device action: playing stays playing, paused stays paused, at the same position

steps.title: Design the queue: next, previous, shuffle, repeat
hints: Store an **order** array of indices into the song list. Shuffle permutes the order, not the songs.
What should happen to the current song when shuffle is turned on? And when it's turned off again?
checklist: next() for each repeat mode, separating automatic advance from a user skip
previous() restarts the song if more than ~3s in
Shuffle with Fisher–Yates, current song stays current
Un-shuffle returns to the original order at the same song

steps.title: Extensibility and concurrency
hints: Who else wants to know the song changed? Lock screen, scrobbler, lyrics panel…
The audio thread fires "track ended" at the same moment the user taps Next. Trace what happens.
Each device SDK has a different API. What pattern makes them all look like one `AudioOutput`?
checklist: Observer for now-playing / scrobbling listeners
Adapter for outputs (speaker, Bluetooth, cast), with a sketch of one adapter
Command for controls from keyboard, headset and remote
The track-ended vs. Next race and a fix (lock plus session token, or a single event loop)
Device disconnect: serialised with everything else, pause first, then fall back to the speaker

steps.title: Code the core
hints: Write `PlayQueue` first and make it pure (no audio, no threads). It's the part with real logic.
Then the three state classes, and finally `Player`, which just delegates.
For devices: `moveOutput` reads the old position, stops the old output, then `prepare`s the new one. Let each state decide whether to `resume()`.
checklist: PlayQueue with next/previous/shuffle and an index-based order
State classes returning the next state
Player delegating to state and queue under one lock
Listeners notified on song and state changes
DeviceManager, one adapter, and Player.selectDevice / deviceDisconnected

steps.title: Answer the follow-ups
hints: Name the class that changes and the classes that don't.
Several of these are new *states* or new *listeners*. Spotting that is the point.
checklist: Crossfade / gapless
Ads between songs on the free tier
Play next / add to queue
Offline downloads
Multi-room playback (Composite output)
